note: Generated by make-vectors.js. Frames are hex. JSON payloads are compact UTF-8; a receiver parses them and never compares their bytes, except where a case says exact. Base64 is standard, padded.

secretFile.rule: 64 lowercase hex characters, optionally one trailing newline; the secret is the 32 bytes they encode

handshake.msRule: HMAC-SHA256(secret, "ch-server" || p || nc || ns): the label as ASCII bytes, p the HELLO protocol as one byte, nc and ns as their 32 raw bytes

tokenMac.rule: HMAC-SHA256(secret, "ch-token" || the token's UTF-8 bytes), sent base64

credentialMac.name: PACK_VAR_ALPHA
credentialMac.rule: HMAC-SHA256(secret, "ch-cred" || the variable's name || 0x00 || the value's UTF-8 bytes), sent standard base64 as credentials[name]

credentialsMalformed.rule: on the first client frame, any of these as credentials is own-runtime (conditions-failed), never shared: not an object, over 32 entries, a name not ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$, a value not the standard base64 of exactly 32 bytes

requestToRuntime.rule: exact: header {"seq": n}, then the client line's bytes without its newline

oddIdToRuntime.rule: the id 1e2 is kept as its bytes, 1e2; matching is by seq only

clientResponseToRuntime.rule: an object with an id and no method is a response: no header, no seq, nothing kept, never crash-answered

nonStringMethod.rule: an id and a method of any type is a request: the shim gives it a seq; the runtime answers with an error

escapedIdKey.rule: member names compare after unescaping: "i\u0064" is id, so it is a request

loneSurrogateKey.rule: a shim parser that refuses the lone surrogate sends it with no header; the runtime, whose JSON.parse accepts it and finds an id, never dispatches it and answers -32600 with id 10
loneSurrogateKey.runtimeAnswer: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"the line was not framed as a request"}}

invalidUtf8.rule: invalid UTF-8: not JSON to the shim (no header); the runtime decodes fatally and answers a parse error, id null, and nothing runs
invalidUtf8.runtimeAnswer: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"parse error: the line is not UTF-8"}}

replyToShim.rule: exact: the shim writes the bytes after the header, then one newline

unmatchedReplyToShim.rule: a seq the shim does not hold: written to the client anyway, nothing recorded

clientNoToken.rule: token null: the environment chooses no token, which is not a failure

clientFailed.json: {"op":"client","status":"failed","why":"the conditions check timed out after 10 s"}
clientFailed.rule: as the first client frame: the runtime answers own-runtime (conditions-failed); as an answer to conditions?: no

clientCredentials.rule: credentials: the pack credentials the client environment chooses, by the installed packs' declared names (never the GitHub ones, which token covers), each credentialMac; absent or {}: none chosen. On the first client frame only: one whose hash is unlike the runtime's own for that name, or that the runtime has no value for, is own-runtime (credential)

startLock.rule: ch-local lib/lock.js: created whole (temporary file, hard link), {pid, host, at} and a newline; heartbeat 15 s; gone after 2 min or a dead pid on this host; .break taken exclusively, stale after 10 s

shimJson.rule: 0600 and trust-checked as the secret; node and chLocal absolute; env only the allowlist (PATH, HOME or USERPROFILE, LANG, TMPDIR on POSIX; SystemRoot, TEMP, TMP, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA on Windows), string values; any other key refused, naming it

failedJson.rule: exactly {v, at, exit, signal, reason}: v 1; at a positive safe integer; exit a safe integer or null; signal ^SIG[A-Z0-9]+$ or null; reason "restarts-exhausted" or "never-listened"; no key extra, missing or twice; read with daemon.json's trust checks, at most 512 bytes; fresh when now - 600000 <= at <= now + 60000; a fresh valid file means no daemon is spawned and the session runs its own runtime; anything else is ignored

accepted.why: now
the past edge
the future edge

failedJson.stderr: the shared runtime failed (<reason>); this session runs its own

sessionCantFallBackAnswer.rule: exact apart from the id: a mid-session fallback refused because the shim holds a record (its session's tightenings would be lost); each held and later request gets it, then the shim exits non-zero
sessionCantFallBackAnswer.json: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"countinghouse's shared runtime failed, and this session's tightened settings can't move to a runtime of its own: restart the session","data":{"countinghouse/code":"SESSION_CANT_FALL_BACK","retryable":false}}}
sessionCantFallBackAnswer.stderr: the shared runtime failed (<reason>), and this session's tightened settings can't move to a runtime of its own: restart the session

sessionTighteningsLostAnswer.rule: exact apart from the id: a session refused because the shim lost one of its tightenings (a record it could not keep, so a new session cannot be given it back; or the runtime said it could not keep them, or did not say, after a replay or a restore); each held and later request gets it, then the shim exits non-zero. A mid-session failure, and a session that cannot share, keep sessionCantFallBackAnswer
sessionTighteningsLostAnswer.json: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"countinghouse couldn't keep the settings this session tightened, so the session stops: restart it","data":{"countinghouse/code":"SESSION_TIGHTENINGS_LOST","retryable":false}}}
sessionTighteningsLostAnswer.stderr: ch-shim: the runtime couldn't resume this session, and a setting this session tightened couldn't be kept, so the session stops: restart it

secretFiles.refusedRule: anything but exactly 64 lowercase hex characters with at most one trailing newline, and a file that is a symlink, not owned by the user, or not 0600 (on Windows, not private by the privateProblem rule)

tooLongLineAnswer.rule: a client line over maxToRuntime - 4096: discarded to its newline, never forwarded; the shim answers with this, <limit> the bound in bytes
tooLongLineAnswer.json: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"the request is larger than countinghouse accepts (8388608 bytes)"}}

clientFromChildLine.rule: the child's one JSON object spliced into {"op":"client"}; "seq" added only when answering conditions?

clientFromBadChildLine.rule: anything but exactly one valid JSON object line becomes a failed client frame; why is the shim's own text
clientFromBadChildLine.opOrSeq: a child line with its own "op" or "seq" member would make duplicate keys once spliced, so it is failed too ("the child's line names op or seq")

drainOverflowAnswer.rule: exact apart from the id: a request held past the drain bound (64 requests, or maxToRuntime in all), which never reached the runtime
drainOverflowAnswer.json: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"countinghouse's runtime restarted before this was sent; the call did not run","data":{"countinghouse/code":"RUNTIME_RESTARTED","retryable":true,"mayHaveRun":false}}}

tooLargeAnswer.rule: exact apart from the id; sent with the request's seq instead of an M over maxToShim
tooLargeAnswer.json: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"the answer is larger than this connection carries","data":{"countinghouse/code":"OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE","retryable":false}}}

conditionsWhy.rule: on a status-ok client line whose conditions is "no", an optional why: exactly {reason} or {reason, at}. reason is one of reasons; at is "~/" and a path under the user's home, its segments split on "/" with none empty and none "..", no backslash anywhere (a separator on Windows), at most 200 characters, with no character of hiddenClass (control, line-separator, bidi, zero-width, soft-hyphen, interlinear, tag, variation-selector, filler, lone-surrogate). A path outside the home is never sent. A why that breaks the rule is ignored (the refusal says no why), never shown

accepted.why: a hook in the user's settings
a plugin with a hook
a directory whose name starts with two dots is still under the home
a reason with no place

refused.why: a path that leaves the home by ..
a path that leaves the home by a later ..
a variation selector in the path
a Hangul filler in the path
a bidi override in the path
a tag character in the path
a path that is not a string
a key beside reason and at
a backslash, a separator on Windows, where split on "/" sees no ..
an empty segment after ~/, which some path joins read as absolute
an empty segment inside the path

githubTokenPrecedence.rule: start (a per-session runtime) takes the first of: the client's COUNTINGHOUSE_GITHUB_TOKEN, the stored token, gh auth token, the client's GITHUB_TOKEN. The daemon's runtime, which no client environment reaches, takes the stored token, else gh's, at its start. The conditions check sends the keyed hash of the token start would choose, except that a gh login is sent as null (the daemon has it too): so token is mac(env), mac(stored), null or mac(GITHUB_TOKEN). The session shares when token is null (the daemon's, whatever it holds), or when token is the hash of the token the daemon holds; otherwise own-runtime (token). A stored token that fails its file checks counts as none

cases.why: nothing anywhere
gh only
a stored token, the daemon started on it
a stored token added while the daemon runs on gh's: its own runtime until the daemon restarts
the client sets COUNTINGHOUSE_GITHUB_TOKEN beside a stored one
GITHUB_TOKEN beside a gh login chooses nothing
GITHUB_TOKEN beside a stored token chooses nothing
GITHUB_TOKEN with neither a stored token nor gh
a stored token removed while the daemon still runs on it: null is the daemon's, until its restart (the restart request)
a stored token whose file fails its checks counts as none

moduleMessages.rule: load names one top-level module (name) and reload one or more (names), each by its package name, with dirs: the absolute directory of each module of their closures, by package name, 1 to 64; credentials (optional) is the per-module allowance of the version 2 --remoteCredentials file, each environment name a slot, each package one dirs names. unload names one top-level module; its notice is told once, as given, on the next result of any tool, unless it carries reason: "off" (the module turned off), the runtime serves the settings tool (the single-identity profile with --settingsFile) and its settings file holds enabled.<name> false, when it tells every session its own off text instead: what went with it (the callers loaded at that unload; one unloaded before it is told by its own unload) and the one way back, at a terminal. With reason: "calls" and because: <the package it went with>, on such a runtime whose settings file holds enabled.<because> false, it tells "<name> unloaded: it calls <because>, which is turned off for all your sessions (turning <because> on brings it back)." reason and because are optional and not checked: any other value, or none, is the notice as given. A module-form message carries no scenario, pack, global or remoteCredentials. notice: module a package name or null, and text. reread: what is module-settings or held-back (the --heldBackFile list), and it carries nothing but id, type and what. module-stopped (the runtime to ch-local, unasked, no id): name, code, when start or restart

accepted.why: a load
a load with credentials
a reload of two names that share a part
a reload of three names over two shared parts
an unload
an unload of a module turned off, said so: the runtime tells every session its full off text
an unload of a caller, with the module turned off it went with: the runtime tells its line with the way back

message.name: @countinghouse/ch-pack-other
message.notice: ch-pack-other unloaded: it calls ch-pack-example, which is turned off

accepted.why: a reread of the module settings
a reread of the held-back list (--heldBackFile; countinghouse_overview)
a notice about a module
a notice about no module
the runtime stopped a module for good

refused.why: a directory that is not absolute
a name that is not a package name
a credentials environment name that is not a slot
a notice with a leftover pack field
a reread of anything but the module settings or the held-back list
a reread with a field beside id, type and what

heldBackFile.rule: exactly {v: 1, modules: [...], launcher?}; at most 256 modules, none named twice; each exactly {name, reason, root?, via?, code?}; name an npm package name not starting with - or ~; reason one of credential, off, ceiling, missing, pin, withdrawn, stopped, restart, changed, gone, sandbox, collision, refused, calls (changed, gone, sandbox, collision and refused are an own module's); code exactly on refused, the runtime's code for its refusal, [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}; root only on calls, one of credential, off, ceiling, missing, pin, withdrawn or not-installed; via exactly when root is, or on collision (the other module's package name): a package name (not starting with - or ~), or for not-installed the callee's declared name (1 to 64 characters, no / or . or control character). The file is a regular file, one name, no link, 0600 (or a private ACL on Windows), this user's own, at most 65536 bytes.

accepted.why: none held back
each reason
an own module whose name another module uses: via names it
an own module this release's runtime refuses, with its code
a part blocked by a credential
a part turned off by the ceiling
a callee nothing installed, by its declared name

refused.why: a name read as an option
a name read as a home
a root on an entry that is not calls
a credential's via that is not a package name
a code that is not one
an own module's reason as a root
gone as a root (an own module's)
via on a reason that takes none

restoreRows.rule: a row is exactly {session, resume, state}: session 32 lowercase hex, resume 64 lowercase hex (SHA-256 of the resume token), state exactly {overrides, locks, formsLeft}, or those and unanswered (the distinct kinds the session has left one form unanswered of: none of them locked, and only with a form spent, formsLeft under 3); overrides at most 2 (one per cap), one per name, each exactly {name, value, loosening, over, version}: a cap has an integer value within the settings tool's bounds (maxOutputBytes 1048576 to 268435456, requestTimeout 5000 to 120000), version null, and over a positive integer when loosening is true, else null; nothing else is overridden (a pack's or a module's on/off is never a session's own: a well-formed pack.<n> override from before M5a, with a boolean value, over null and a semver version, is dropped from its row, the rest of the row taken and its session told once; any other pack.<n> override refuses the restore); locks distinct kinds of maxOutputBytes, requestTimeout, enabled, module (every enabled.<module> is the one kind enabled, every module.<package>.<setting> the one kind module; the kind pack, from a runtime before M5b, is taken as enabled in locks, unanswered and declines, deduped, a kind both locked and unanswered after it staying locked, and said once (mapped); a kind this runtime has none of, of a kind's shape (a letter, then letters and digits, at most 64), in a row's locks or unanswered is dropped from it when nothing else in the row refuses, the rest of the row (its known locks, its forms) taken; a decline of such a kind is dropped (kindsDropped); anything else in a kind's place refuses the restore); formsLeft an integer 0 to 3; at most 64 KiB as JSON. The restore message is exactly {id, type: "restore", sessions, declines, reset}: reset lists the sessions (each a row's) that lost loosenings in a handoff, to be told so

dropped.why: a well-formed pack override from before M5a: dropped; the session's cap override, locks and forms kept

mapped.why: a lock of the kind pack: locked enabled, the session's cap override kept
the kinds pack and enabled both locked: enabled once
an unanswered form of the kind pack: unanswered enabled
pack unanswered and enabled locked: the lock stays, nothing unanswered of it (unanswered, left empty, is gone)
pack locked and enabled unanswered: the lock stays, nothing unanswered of it

kindsDropped.why: a lock of a kind this runtime has none of, beside a known one: the known lock and the forms kept
an unanswered form of a kind this runtime has none of: the other unanswered kept
an unanswered form of an unknown kind alone: unanswered, left empty, is gone; the spent forms kept

refused.why: a kind both locked and unanswered
an unanswered form with no form spent
a lock of the kind pack twice
a lock that is not a kind's shape
a row of an unknown kind that refuses for another reason
a pack override not of the old shape (no version)
a cap loosening with no over

topLevelModules.rule: a module is top-level when it is the scenario of a pack in packs: of that pack's modules (in their order), the first that modules gives role "scenario", else the pack's first module; and only when modules holds it. Every other module in modules is a part, whatever its role, and has no enabled.<module>. Only own properties are read (Object.hasOwn), so a name like "constructor" is a name like any other

cases.why: a pack's scenario and its part
the scenario listed after its part
a pack with no module of role scenario: its first module
a module of role null in no pack is a part
a module of role scenario in no pack is a part
a pack's scenario that modules does not hold: none
a scenario of one pack that another lists too: top-level once
two of role scenario in one pack: the first
a pack with no modules
a pack listing "constructor" first, which modules does not hold: none, the other a part
a module named "constructor", held and of role scenario: top-level
a pack named "constructor"

historyCut.rule: fields old, new, asked and kept of a module.* history line: a string of more than 64 code points is written as its first 64 code points, with <field>Sha256 beside it, the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 of JSON.stringify(the WHOLE value); any other value, and a string of 64 code points or fewer, is written whole with no Sha256 field. A reader compares a recorded <field>Sha256 with the SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(the value it holds)

cases.why: 65 code points, the last one not ASCII: cut to 64, hashed whole
exactly 64 code points: whole, no hash
64 code points of which one is outside the BMP (JS length 65): whole, a surrogate pair never split
65 code points ending outside the BMP: cut before the pair
a quote and a backslash: hashed as JSON, escapes and all
a number: never cut
a boolean: never cut

seqRule: the shim counts seq from 1 for its whole life; it never restarts on a reconnect or a resume

crashAnswer.rule: exact apart from the id, which is the request's own
crashAnswer.json: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"countinghouse's runtime restarted before answering; the call may have run","data":{"countinghouse/code":"RUNTIME_RESTARTED","retryable":true,"mayHaveRun":true}}}

cases.name: a PROVE whose ms is wrong
cases.given: HELLO sent; PROVE arrives with ms = msHex with its first byte xor 0x01
cases.expect: the shim closes the connection, sends no AUTH and relays no client byte

cases.name: a frame over its kind's cap
cases.given: any frame whose length field exceeds the cap (handshake 4096, C 65536, M as WELCOME says)
cases.expect: the receiver closes without reading the payload

cases.name: bytes before HELLO
cases.given: more than 512 bytes from a connection that has sent no complete HELLO

cases.name: a wrong AUTH
cases.given: AUTH with mc of another secret
cases.expect: the runtime sends REFUSED {code: "BAD_PROOF"} and closes

cases.name: a resume while the session is live
cases.given: AUTH with the resumeToken of a session that still has a connection
cases.expect: REFUSED {code: "RESUME_REFUSED"}; the shim then opens a new session and replays its records

cases.name: an M frame before WELCOME
cases.given: an M or C frame from the shim before WELCOME

cases.name: a client line with a newline inside a string
cases.given: the line is split only on the byte 0x0a, which JSON text never carries unescaped
cases.expect: each line is one M frame

cases.name: client lines before settled
cases.given: WELCOME, then the client writes a request before settled arrives
cases.expect: the shim holds it and forwards it after settled; on own-runtime it hands it to the per-session runtime

cases.name: a wrong ms after a restart
cases.given: PROVE fails, then daemon.json and the secret are rewritten
cases.expect: the shim re-reads both and attaches within its 20 s

cases.name: a mid-session fallback holding a record
cases.given: a live session with one record loses the daemon, reattaches and finds a fresh failed.json
cases.expect: no per-session runtime is started; each held request is answered sessionCantFallBackAnswer, the stderr line is said, and the shim exits non-zero

cases.name: a mid-session fallback with no record
cases.given: a live legacy session with no record loses the daemon and finds a fresh failed.json
cases.expect: the shim starts own-runtime, replays its initialize and notifications/initialized first, drops that answer, then sends the held lines

cases.name: conditions? unanswered
cases.given: the shim sends no client frame for 12 s after conditions? (it gives the child 10 s)
cases.expect: the runtime counts it as no for that form: no form
